documents.title: Passkeys, two-factor and active sessions

chunks.heading: Signing in
chunks.headingPath: Passkeys, two-factor and active sessions › Signing in
chunks.text:
Sign in with the email you registered, with Google or GitHub if you signed up
that way, or with a passkey. "Sign in with a passkey" appears where your browser
and device support one. If a sign-in or verification email has not arrived,
check the spam folder before requesting another.

chunks.heading: Second factors
chunks.headingPath: Passkeys, two-factor and active sessions › Second factors
chunks.text:
Settings, Security manages passkeys and two-factor authentication. Passkeys sign
you in; an authenticator app code (TOTP) with recovery backup codes is the
supported second factor. Hardware security keys, SMS MFA and trusted-device
lists are not part of the current account contract, so they are not offered
rather than silently ignored.

Keep the backup codes somewhere separate from the phone holding the
authenticator. At sign-in the second-factor screen accepts either the
authenticator code or one of your backup codes.

chunks.heading: Password
chunks.headingPath: Passkeys, two-factor and active sessions › Password
chunks.text:
The same page changes your password. A password that fails the common-password
check is refused with "That password is too common." A forgotten password is
reset from the sign-in screen with **Forgot password?**.

chunks.heading: Active sessions
chunks.headingPath: Passkeys, two-factor and active sessions › Active sessions
chunks.text:
Settings, Account lists every signed-in session with its device, browser,
location, when it was created and when it was last active, and marks the one
you are using. **Revoke** signs that device out immediately; it has to sign in
again to regain access. If the list is truncated it says how many of the total
it is showing.

**Log out of all devices** ends every session including this one, so you will
need to sign in again. It asks first and names that consequence.

A session also ends on its own once it reaches its maximum age, counted from
when you signed in rather than from your last request, so a session that is in
constant use still ends and asks you to sign in again. The maximum is 30 days.

Sessions are reported by your account provider across devices. Revoke anything
you do not recognise.

chunks.heading: Your identifiers
chunks.headingPath: Passkeys, two-factor and active sessions › Your identifiers
chunks.text:
Settings, Account shows your **User ID**, and an **Organization ID** when the
account belongs to a workspace. Support asks for these when investigating an
issue; they identify the account, they are not secrets that grant access.

chunks.heading: API keys
chunks.headingPath: Passkeys, two-factor and active sessions › API keys
chunks.text:
API keys are managed from Settings, Account under **API keys**. Regenerating a
key invalidates the previous one immediately, so update anything using it.

documents.title: Accounts and signing in

chunks.heading: Signing in
chunks.headingPath: Accounts and signing in › Signing in
chunks.text:
Open [Sign in](https://agiworkforce.com/login) and use the email address or sign-in provider associated
with your account. Follow the password or email-code option shown on screen.

If a verification code has not arrived, check your spam folder and confirm the
email address, then use **Resend code** when it becomes available. If you forgot
your account password, choose **Forgot password?** on the password screen.

chunks.heading: Using AGI on several devices
chunks.headingPath: Accounts and signing in › Using AGI on several devices
chunks.text:
To reopen saved web conversations on another device, sign in to the web app with
the same account and select the same workspace. Personal and Enterprise workspaces
are separate, so check the workspace menu if expected conversations are missing.

Check [Downloads](https://agiworkforce.com/download) for the current release status of other clients before
trying to install them. Local-mode conversations stay on the device that created
them. Temporary chats do not appear in saved history.

chunks.heading: CLI provider credentials are separate
chunks.headingPath: Accounts and signing in › CLI provider credentials are separate
chunks.text:
The released CLI stores provider keys in the operating system credential store.
Those keys are separate from your AGI account credential. Desktop accepts no
provider key, and VS Code BYOK is coming soon.

chunks.heading: Contacting support
chunks.headingPath: Accounts and signing in › Contacting support
chunks.text:
Send support requests to contact@agiworkforce.com. The support page lists the
available channels and any plan-specific response commitments.

documents.title: Run a task with AGI Work

chunks.heading: What AGI Work is
chunks.headingPath: Run a task with AGI Work › What AGI Work is
chunks.text:
AGI Work is the mode for a task rather than a question: you describe a
multi-step job and what it should deliver, and the session plans, works and
produces files. The composer switches between **Chat**, for quick questions and
conversation, and **AGI Work**, where the placeholder asks you to describe a
multi-step task and what it should deliver.

chunks.heading: Watching a session
chunks.headingPath: Run a task with AGI Work › Watching a session
chunks.text:
A running session opens a dock beside the conversation with four sections:

- **Progress**: the steps the session planned. Before it plans, the section says
  steps appear once the session plans its work.
- **Sources**: the pages the session reads as it searches.
- **Outputs**: the files the session produced, each with **Open** and
  **Download**.
- **Context**: the connectors the session used, empty until one is called.

A plain chat gets the same dock titled **Chat details**, listing the files
created in that chat, and does not claim to be a Work session.

chunks.heading: Approvals during a session
chunks.headingPath: Run a task with AGI Work › Approvals during a session
chunks.text:
What a session may do on its own follows your tool-approval default. On the
default, **Ask before every action**, every connector, plugin and tool action
waits for you, reads included. If you switched to **Run read-only actions
without asking**, the session shows a notice saying so: read-only actions run
without asking, and anything that writes, runs code, searches the web, or
reaches outside AGI, including your connectors, pauses for your approval.

chunks.heading: Finding past sessions
chunks.headingPath: Run a task with AGI Work › Finding past sessions
chunks.text:
**Work history** at the tasks page lists previous sessions. Opening one and
choosing to run it again loads that session's goal into a new AGI Work chat for
you to review and send, rather than re-running it unattended.

chunks.heading: Availability
chunks.headingPath: Run a task with AGI Work › Availability
chunks.text:
AGI Work is one of the features a workspace administrator can turn off for a
managed workspace, and higher-capacity work is a paid-plan feature. The pricing
page carries the current details.

documents.title: Artifacts: documents and code AGI writes for you

chunks.heading: What an artifact is
chunks.headingPath: Artifacts: documents and code AGI writes for you › What an artifact is
chunks.text:
When an answer produces a document, a piece of code or a rendered page rather
than a paragraph, it opens as an artifact in a panel beside the conversation.
The panel can be opened and closed from the conversation, or with
Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+A, and has a fullscreen view.

chunks.heading: Editing one
chunks.headingPath: Artifacts: documents and code AGI writes for you › Editing one
chunks.text:
Edits you make in the panel are saved as new versions, and earlier versions can
be restored. **Duplicate** makes an independent copy, confirmed with
"Duplicated. Edits here no longer touch the original." **Save to project** files
it into a project's knowledge.

If someone else changed the same artifact first, the panel keeps your work and
says so: their version is shown and your edit is kept as the latest version.
Nothing is silently discarded.

chunks.heading: Getting a copy out
chunks.headingPath: Artifacts: documents and code AGI writes for you › Getting a copy out
chunks.text:
**Copy artifact** puts the source on the clipboard. **Download file** and
**Download image** save it. From the Library, an artifact exports as PDF or
Word.

chunks.heading: Publishing
chunks.headingPath: Artifacts: documents and code AGI writes for you › Publishing
chunks.text:
Publishing an artifact gives it a link. The audience works like a shared
conversation: anyone with the link, or your workspace only, and the panel
confirms which is in force. Changing it later asks first ("Make this public
again?", "Limit this to your workspace?").

Settings holds a **Published artifacts** list with **Unpublish artifact** on
each one. Unpublishing stops the link working.

chunks.heading: When a preview will not render
chunks.headingPath: Artifacts: documents and code AGI writes for you › When a preview will not render
chunks.text:
"Inline preview unavailable" or "Image preview unavailable" means the panel
cannot render that content in place, not that the artifact is damaged. Download
it and open it locally.

documents.title: Plans, upgrading, and cancelling

chunks.heading: Where billing lives
chunks.headingPath: Plans, upgrading, and cancelling › Where billing lives
chunks.text:
Settings, Billing shows your current plan, when the period ends, your payment
method, your invoices and your credit balance. **Manage billing** opens the
billing portal where the card and the subscription itself are changed.

chunks.heading: Upgrading
chunks.headingPath: Plans, upgrading, and cancelling › Upgrading
chunks.text:
**Upgrade plan** lists the plans available to you and starts checkout. Local
mode and BYOK are free and need no plan at all. Managed cloud plans differ in
usage capacity and in which features they include: projects, custom MCP
connections, concurrent responses, sandboxes, connector tools and scheduled
tasks all scale with the plan. The pricing page carries the current prices,
regional prices and per-plan limits.

chunks.heading: Cancelling
chunks.headingPath: Plans, upgrading, and cancelling › Cancelling
chunks.text:
On a plan billed through the web, **Cancel plan** in Settings, Billing opens the
billing portal at the cancellation flow. Once cancellation is scheduled the
period row changes from "Renews on" to "Cancels on", and access continues to
that date.

chunks.heading: Subscriptions bought in an app store
chunks.headingPath: Plans, upgrading, and cancelling › Subscriptions bought in an app store
chunks.text:
If the subscription was bought through Apple or Google, AGI cannot change it.
The page says so and points you at the store: "Change or cancel this
subscription with Apple before starting web billing", and the equivalent for
Google Play. Cancel there first if you want to move to web billing.

chunks.heading: Plans your organization pays for
chunks.headingPath: Plans, upgrading, and cancelling › Plans your organization pays for
chunks.text:
On a workspace-managed plan the controls are read-only: "This plan is managed by
your organization. Contact an administrator to change it", and invoices are
provided by the organization rather than shown here.

chunks.heading: Invoices
chunks.headingPath: Plans, upgrading, and cancelling › Invoices
chunks.text:
Invoices appear once you are billed on a paid plan. Before the first cycle
closes the list says so rather than showing an error.

chunks.heading: When billing will not let you change plans
chunks.headingPath: Plans, upgrading, and cancelling › When billing will not let you change plans
chunks.text:
- "Billing ownership is not verified. Refresh your account before changing
  plans." Reload and sign in again.
- "Resolve the current billing status in Manage billing before changing plans."
  A payment needs attention first; the payment-failure page lists what to check.

documents.title: Add your own provider API key (BYOK)

chunks.heading: What BYOK means here
chunks.headingPath: Add your own provider API key (BYOK) › What BYOK means here
chunks.text:
BYOK is "bring your own key". The released CLI accepts provider API keys today,
and VS Code BYOK is coming soon. AGI sends requests directly to the provider you
selected. Usage is billed by that provider, not by AGI, and AGI adds no markup.
Web, Mobile, Desktop and Chrome do not accept provider keys; each runs on your AGI
account.

chunks.heading: Adding a key
chunks.headingPath: Add your own provider API key (BYOK) › Adding a key
chunks.text:
1. Run `agi login <provider>`, such as `agi login anthropic`.
2. Paste the provider API key when the CLI prompts for it.
3. Run `agi auth-status` to confirm the saved provider. The CLI stores the secret
   in the OS credential store.

A bare `agi login` signs in to AGI managed cloud. It does not prompt for a
provider API key.

chunks.heading: Anthropic
chunks.headingPath: Add your own provider API key (BYOK) › Anthropic
chunks.text: Create an API key in the Anthropic console, then run `agi login anthropic`.

chunks.heading: OpenAI
chunks.headingPath: Add your own provider API key (BYOK) › OpenAI
chunks.text: Create an API key in the OpenAI platform dashboard, then run `agi login openai`.

chunks.heading: Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints
chunks.headingPath: Add your own provider API key (BYOK) › Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints
chunks.text:
The released CLI accepts the provider names listed by `agi login --help`. Custom
OpenAI-compatible endpoints remain subject to the CLI's current configuration and
provider support.

chunks.heading: VS Code release state
chunks.headingPath: Add your own provider API key (BYOK) › VS Code release state
chunks.text:
The VS Code extension has a private SecretStorage-backed key flow in the codebase,
but no VSIX has been published yet. The public setup instructions will apply when
that release is available.

chunks.heading: BYOK keys are never used for managed cloud
chunks.headingPath: Add your own provider API key (BYOK) › BYOK keys are never used for managed cloud
chunks.text:
Managed cloud runs on AGI-operated provider access, and BYOK credentials are
explicitly refused on that path. The two remain separate trust boundaries.

documents.title: Start, steer and manage a chat

chunks.heading: Start a new chat
chunks.headingPath: Start, steer and manage a chat › Start a new chat
chunks.text:
Open the chat surface and type. A new conversation begins with the first
message you send; nothing is created before that. Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+O starts a new
conversation from anywhere in the app. Cmd/Ctrl+B shows or hides the sidebar.

chunks.heading: Choose how the answer is written
chunks.headingPath: Start, steer and manage a chat › Choose how the answer is written
chunks.text:
The composer carries a **Response style** control with Default, Concise,
Detailed, Technical and Creative, plus a response-length control. You can save
your own style by naming it and giving it an instruction, or by pasting a
writing sample for AGI to match. Custom styles can be edited and deleted from
the same menu.

chunks.heading: Attach files and tools
chunks.headingPath: Start, steer and manage a chat › Attach files and tools
chunks.text:
The **+** button beside the composer attaches files, adds a project or folder as
scope, and lists your connectors. Typing `/` opens the command menu:
`/search` searches the web, `/think` asks for extended reasoning, `/image`
generates an image, `/code` runs code in a sandbox. `/browser`, `/terminal` and
`/database` appear only on surfaces whose capabilities allow them.

chunks.heading: Change a message after you sent it
chunks.headingPath: Start, steer and manage a chat › Change a message after you sent it
chunks.text:
Hover a message to reveal its actions. You can edit your own message and send
it again, copy a response, give a good or bad rating, and regenerate the answer.
Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+R regenerates the last response and Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+C copies it.
Regenerating keeps the earlier answer as a variant; the pager under the message
steps between variants, and a variant can be deleted from there.

chunks.heading: Rename, archive and delete
chunks.headingPath: Start, steer and manage a chat › Rename, archive and delete
chunks.text:
The conversation title menu renames a chat. Archiving moves it out of the
sidebar without deleting anything, and Settings holds an **Archived chats** list
that restores a chat or moves it to **Recently deleted**. A deleted chat stays
there until you restore it; the product does not currently offer permanent chat
deletion separately from deleting your account.

chunks.heading: When a chat will not load
chunks.headingPath: Start, steer and manage a chat › When a chat will not load
chunks.text:
The failure notice says "Chat could not be displayed" and offers **Try again**.
If the browser is offline it says "You are offline" instead. In both cases your
messages are already saved, so retrying or opening a different conversation
loses nothing.

documents.title: The Chrome extension

chunks.heading: Availability
chunks.headingPath: The Chrome extension › Availability
chunks.text:
The Chrome extension, AGI Browser Companion, is not published yet. The Chrome
page carries its status and a notify list; there is no Web Store listing to
install from today.

chunks.heading: What it is being built to do
chunks.headingPath: The Chrome extension › What it is being built to do
chunks.text:
It opens AGI in a browser side panel next to the page you are reading, with a
keyboard command to open the panel and another to capture the current page into
the conversation. Its host permissions are limited to agiworkforce.com, the AGI
API and localhost, so it talks to AGI and to nothing else by default.

chunks.heading: Browser automation
chunks.headingPath: The Chrome extension › Browser automation
chunks.text:
The composer's `/browser` command exists only on surfaces whose capabilities
allow browser automation, which is what the extension provides. Anything that
drives a page is a write action under the approval rules: on the default
setting it asks before every action, and even on the read-only-auto setting it
still asks, because driving a browser is not a read.

chunks.heading: Managed cloud from the extension
chunks.headingPath: The Chrome extension › Managed cloud from the extension
chunks.text:
Managed cloud access from the Chrome extension is part of the higher paid tiers.
The extension does not accept provider keys: web, mobile, desktop and Chrome all
run on your AGI account, while BYOK is a CLI and VS Code capability.

chunks.heading: Until it ships
chunks.headingPath: The Chrome extension › Until it ships
chunks.text:
The web app runs in the same browser and covers everything except the
page-capture and side-panel workflow.

documents.title: Connectors and MCP

chunks.heading: What connectors do
chunks.headingPath: Connectors and MCP › What connectors do
chunks.text:
Connectors let AGI call an external system on your behalf, reading a repository,
querying a service, or running a tool exposed over MCP (Model Context Protocol).
Every connector is scoped to your own account.

chunks.heading: Adding a connector
chunks.headingPath: Connectors and MCP › Adding a connector
chunks.text:
Open the connectors page, choose the connector, and complete its authorization flow.
Custom MCP endpoints can be added with their own URL.

chunks.heading: Tool permissions
chunks.headingPath: Connectors and MCP › Tool permissions
chunks.text:
When a connector's tool runs for the first time, AGI asks for approval. Choosing
"Always allow" saves that verdict so the same tool can run without prompting again.

chunks.heading: Removing a connector
chunks.headingPath: Connectors and MCP › Removing a connector
chunks.text:
Removing a connector deactivates it and clears the saved "Always allow" tool
permissions at the same time, so a later reconnect starts from a clean approval
state. AGI asks the provider to revoke every account you connected through it,
not only the one AGI treated as the default, and deletes the credentials it held
for them.

chunks.heading: Custom MCP connections and plans
chunks.headingPath: Connectors and MCP › Custom MCP connections and plans
chunks.text:
The number of custom MCP connections available depends on your plan. Current plan
details live on the pricing page.

documents.title: Delete your account, or cancel a scheduled deletion

chunks.heading: How deletion works
chunks.headingPath: Delete your account, or cancel a scheduled deletion › How deletion works
chunks.text:
Settings, Account carries **Delete account**, marked "This cannot be undone."
Confirming requires typing `DELETE` into the dialog. The dialog states what
happens: your account and all associated data are permanently deleted, you are
signed out now, and erasure runs 24 hours after you confirm.

After you confirm, the dialog shows the date and time the 24 hours are up, and
you are signed out when you continue. That is the earliest moment erasure can
begin, not the moment it finishes: the job that erases accounts runs once a day,
so the work starts on the first daily run after that deadline passes.

chunks.heading: Changing your mind
chunks.headingPath: Delete your account, or cancel a scheduled deletion › Changing your mind
chunks.text:
The 24 hours are a real cancellation window, not a formality. Sign back in
before the deadline and Settings, Account shows **Account deletion scheduled**
with the erasure time and a **Cancel deletion** button. Cancelling keeps the
account active and removes nothing.

Once the window closes the button is gone and the page says the cancellation
window has closed and erasure is already underway.

chunks.heading: Before you confirm
chunks.headingPath: Delete your account, or cancel a scheduled deletion › Before you confirm
chunks.text:
Export your conversations first. The export is a self-service download from
Settings, Privacy, and it cannot be run once the account is gone.

If a paid subscription is attached, cancel or let it lapse separately; billing
is handled in the billing portal, not by the deletion flow.

If you are the only owner of a workspace, the request is refused and nothing is
scheduled. The message names every workspace you own alone, so hand each one to
another owner or delete it first, then try again.

chunks.heading: Deleting conversations without deleting the account
chunks.headingPath: Delete your account, or cancel a scheduled deletion › Deleting conversations without deleting the account
chunks.text:
Settings, Privacy has narrower controls for the workspace you are currently
using. **Archive all chats** moves that workspace's chats out of the sidebar and
can be undone from Archived chats. **Delete all chats** moves that workspace's
active and archived conversations to Recently deleted, where you can restore
them. Both ask first and name the current-workspace scope.

documents.title: Desktop app and CLI

chunks.heading: The CLI
chunks.headingPath: Desktop app and CLI › The CLI
chunks.text:
The AGI CLI is a Rust-native developer agent with resumable sessions, sandboxed
execution, and offline-capable operation through Local mode. The CLI page carries
the current install guide for the `agi` command.

chunks.heading: The desktop app
chunks.headingPath: Desktop app and CLI › The desktop app
chunks.text:
The current Desktop application is an Electron shell for managed-cloud account
work. It does not accept provider keys or run a local model. No Desktop installer
has been published yet; the download page reports release availability instead of
offering an unverified asset.

chunks.heading: What the desktop app adds
chunks.headingPath: Desktop app and CLI › What the desktop app adds
chunks.text:
- A dedicated managed-cloud window for your AGI account.
- Approved-folder workflows and one-step computer-use approvals on supported
  macOS builds.
- The optional Chrome native bridge.

Local and BYOK are available in the released CLI. The CLI's documented local
integrations are Ollama and LM Studio, and `agi login <provider>` stores provider
keys in the OS credential store.

chunks.heading: Managed cloud from developer surfaces
chunks.headingPath: Desktop app and CLI › Managed cloud from developer surfaces
chunks.text:
Desktop itself is managed-cloud-only. Managed cloud access from the CLI, Chrome,
and VS Code depends on release availability and the current plan details shown on
the pricing page.

documents.title: Security review of AGI for an enterprise

chunks.heading: Evaluate before you sign anything
chunks.headingPath: Security review of AGI for an enterprise › Evaluate before you sign anything
chunks.text:
Local mode and BYOK need no contract, no trial and no seat, so a reviewer can
run the product on their own hardware while procurement is still reading. In
Local mode nothing reaches AGI infrastructure at all, which makes it the
cheapest way to assess behaviour without a data-processing conversation.

chunks.heading: What is claimed, and what is not
chunks.headingPath: Security review of AGI for an enterprise › What is claimed, and what is not
chunks.text:
Claims are dated on the trust ledger rather than asserted in prose. Two things
are stated plainly there and worth knowing before you write a questionnaire:

- HIPAA-covered workflows are not offered today.
- No certification body is engaged and no certification date is claimed.
  Anything on the roadmap stays on the roadmap with no date until there is one.

Read the ledger for the current state rather than a sales page, and send the
questionnaire; terms are negotiated against your procurement rather than by
click-through.

chunks.heading: Controls an administrator actually has
chunks.headingPath: Security review of AGI for an enterprise › Controls an administrator actually has
chunks.text:
- Local, BYOK and managed cloud allowed or refused per workspace.
- Public share links and phone sync switched off server side, not by asking
  people not to use them.
- Retention windows, enforced when the workspace owner turns them on, with a
  record of what retention deleted and legal holds that suspend it.
- Feature, model and connector policy, with exceptions scoped to a role, a
  group or a person.
- The route each answer took, printed on every reply, so a claim about where a
  request went is checkable rather than trusted.

chunks.heading: Audit evidence
chunks.headingPath: Security review of AGI for an enterprise › Audit evidence
chunks.text:
The audit trail is an append-only table, newest first, one event per line,
streamed as it is read. An administrator downloads it as JSONL, or has signed
batches drained to a SIEM endpoint every thirty minutes.

chunks.heading: Data residency
chunks.headingPath: Security review of AGI for an enterprise › Data residency
chunks.text:
Hosted data lives in the United States. EU and UK residency hosting is on the
roadmap and is not available today. Local conversations never leave the device
in the first place, which is the residency answer for the strictest cases.

documents.title: Export a copy of your data

chunks.heading: Self-service export
chunks.headingPath: Export a copy of your data › Self-service export
chunks.text:
Settings, Privacy carries **Download all your conversations as JSON**. The
export runs in the browser and downloads a single file named for the day you
ran it. It is a self-service download, not a request you wait on.

chunks.heading: What else you can ask for
chunks.headingPath: Export a copy of your data › What else you can ask for
chunks.text:
The privacy requests page is the formal rights path: review your consent record,
or ask AGI to access, correct or erase your data. Settings links to it directly
so you do not have to find it from a policy page.

chunks.heading: Files and generated media
chunks.headingPath: Export a copy of your data › Files and generated media
chunks.text:
Uploads and generated media are listed in your Library, and in Settings under
the data section, where individual items can be reviewed or deleted. They are
covered by the same rights path as conversations.

chunks.heading: Before you delete your account
chunks.headingPath: Export a copy of your data › Before you delete your account
chunks.text:
Export first. Account deletion erases conversations and account data, and the
export cannot be run afterwards. See the account deletion article for the
timing and the cancellation window.

documents.title: Attach files to a chat

chunks.heading: Attaching a file
chunks.headingPath: Attach files to a chat › Attaching a file
chunks.text:
Use the **+** button beside the composer, drag files onto the conversation, or
paste them from the clipboard. Attachments appear as previews above the
composer, and each one can be removed before you send.

chunks.heading: What a chat can read
chunks.headingPath: Attach files to a chat › What a chat can read
chunks.text:
Images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP), PDFs, plain text and Markdown, CSV, JSON and
notebooks, HTML, CSS, XML, and Word, Excel and PowerPoint documents. Source
files in common languages are accepted as text.

chunks.heading: When a file does not go with the message
chunks.headingPath: Attach files to a chat › When a file does not go with the message
chunks.text:
The composer refuses a file rather than sending your message without it, and the
outgoing turn carries a line naming the file and the reason, so the model knows
an attachment is missing instead of inventing its contents. The reasons you can
see are:

- larger than this chat can send
- not a file type this chat can read
- this message already carries as many files as it can
- this conversation has reached its attachment limit
- removed from your Library, so attach it again
- could not be loaded, so attach it again

If a file is refused for size, convert or split it; if it is refused for type,
paste the contents as text instead.

chunks.heading: Where attachments end up
chunks.headingPath: Attach files to a chat › Where attachments end up
chunks.text:
Files you attach in an ordinary chat are stored in your **Library**, where you
can find, preview, re-attach or delete them. Files attached in a temporary chat
are deliberately kept out of the Library.

chunks.heading: Files AGI creates
chunks.headingPath: Attach files to a chat › Files AGI creates
chunks.text:
Generated images, documents and other outputs appear in the conversation and in
the Library alongside your uploads. In an AGI Work session they also collect in
the session dock under **Outputs**, with **Open** and **Download** on each one.

documents.title: Getting started with AGI

chunks.heading: Create an account and start a chat
chunks.headingPath: Getting started with AGI › Create an account and start a chat
chunks.text:
Sign up at agiworkforce.com, then open the chat surface and send your first message.
A new account can use AGI managed cloud straight away: managed cloud is open by
default, so there is no waitlist and no invite code to redeem.

chunks.heading: The three trust modes
chunks.headingPath: Getting started with AGI › The three trust modes
chunks.text:
AGI runs in three separate trust modes and never silently moves work between them.

- **Local** runs models on your own hardware. The released CLI supports Ollama and
  LM Studio. Local is free and can run offline after the runtime and model are
  installed.
- **BYOK** means you bring your own provider API key. The released CLI supports it
  today, and VS Code BYOK is coming soon. Keys stay in the surface's private
  credential store and traffic goes directly to your provider. Usage is billed by
  the provider, not by AGI, with no markup. BYOK is free.
- **Managed cloud** runs on AGI-operated provider access. It is metered, and
  current plan details live on the pricing page.

Web, Mobile, Desktop and Chrome do not accept provider keys. The current Desktop
application is a managed-cloud account shell and does not run local models.

Moving a conversation from Local to BYOK is always an explicit fork with context
selection, a payload preview, and a visible provider label. It never happens
automatically.

chunks.heading: What to set up first
chunks.headingPath: Getting started with AGI › What to set up first
chunks.text:
1. Pick a trust mode. If you want to stay offline, install the CLI and configure
   Ollama or LM Studio.
2. If you want to use your own provider account, run `agi login <provider>` and
   verify it with `agi auth-status`.
3. If you want AGI to handle provider access for you, use managed cloud on the web.

chunks.heading: Where to go next
chunks.headingPath: Getting started with AGI › Where to go next
chunks.text:
The help index links the six things people ask about most. The FAQ covers the
reasoning behind the trust boundaries.

documents.title: Glossary of AGI terms

chunks.heading: How to read this glossary
chunks.headingPath: Glossary of AGI terms › How to read this glossary
chunks.text:
Each entry gives the term as the product uses it. Where a term has a fuller
article, that article is the authority on the detail; this page exists so a
question phrased with the word alone still finds the right place.

chunks.heading: Trust modes
chunks.headingPath: Glossary of AGI terms › Trust modes
chunks.text:
**Trust mode** is which machine and which provider account runs your request.
AGI runs three and never silently moves work between them.

**Local** runs models on your own hardware through a runtime you install. It is
free, and inference can run offline once the runtime and model are installed.

**BYOK**, "bring your own key", means you supply a provider API key and AGI
sends your requests directly to that provider with it. Keys are encrypted at
rest on your machine. Your provider bills the usage, and AGI adds no markup.
BYOK is free.

**Managed cloud** runs on AGI-operated provider access. It is metered, and it
refuses BYOK credentials by design so the two trust boundaries stay separate.

chunks.heading: Usage and billing terms
chunks.headingPath: Glossary of AGI terms › Usage and billing terms
chunks.text:
**Allowance** is the metered capacity a plan carries for managed cloud. When it
runs out, managed requests stop until it resets; Local and BYOK are unaffected.

**Credits** are a prepaid balance, separate from the allowance, that managed
usage can draw on once the allowance is exhausted.

**Top-up** is a credit purchase for a custom amount in whole dollars.

**Concurrency** is how many responses may be generating at once. Reaching that
ceiling is not the same as exhausting an allowance: it clears as soon as an
in-flight response finishes.

**Auto** is the routing choice that picks a model for you. The free lane is
offered as Auto (free), whose capacity is not guaranteed.

chunks.heading: Chat terms
chunks.headingPath: Glossary of AGI terms › Chat terms
chunks.text:
**Conversation** is a single thread of messages.

**Project** groups conversations around shared context: written instructions,
uploaded knowledge files, and its own memory scope.

**Artifact** is a document, a piece of code or a rendered page that an answer
produces, opened in a panel beside the conversation and versioned as you edit.

**Library** is where past conversations and artifacts are listed.

**Temporary chat** is a conversation that neither reads memory nor writes to
it, and that ignores saved approval verdicts.

**Memory** is what AGI carries between conversations. Persistent memory stores
facts; search past chats instead reads your history at answer time.

chunks.heading: Tools and connectors
chunks.headingPath: Glossary of AGI terms › Tools and connectors
chunks.text:
**Connector** lets AGI call an external system on your behalf. Every connector
is scoped to your own account.

**MCP**, the Model Context Protocol, is the open protocol a connector can use to
expose tools. Custom MCP endpoints can be added with their own URL.

**Tool approval** is the verdict that decides whether a tool may run without
asking. The default is to ask before every action, including reads.

**AGI Work** is the mode for a multi-step task rather than a question: the
session plans, works, and produces files.

chunks.heading: Platform and surface names
chunks.headingPath: Glossary of AGI terms › Platform and surface names
chunks.text:
**Surface** is one of the six places AGI runs: Web, Desktop, CLI, Mobile, VS
Code, and Chrome. A feature can be available on one surface and not another, so
articles name the surface rather than assuming it.

**Web** is agiworkforce.com in a browser.

**Desktop** is the installable desktop app, published for macOS, Windows and
Linux as those releases become available.

**CLI** is the `agi` command, a Rust-native developer agent that runs in a
terminal on macOS, Windows and Linux.

**Mobile** is the phone app, for iOS and Android.

**VS Code** and **Chrome** are the editor extension and the browser extension.

**macOS**, **Windows** and **Linux** are the desktop operating systems;
**iOS** and **Android** are the mobile ones. Support articles tag the platforms
they apply to, so a question about one platform does not answer with another.

documents.title: Installing the desktop and mobile apps

chunks.heading: What is published today
chunks.headingPath: Installing the desktop and mobile apps › What is published today
chunks.text:
The web app and the CLI are available now. The desktop app, the mobile app, the
VS Code extension and the Chrome extension are not published yet. The download
page lists each platform with its status and a notify list: "You're on the list.
We'll email you when a platform has a verified installer to download."

This page will not give you an install command for something that does not have
a release. Anything else would be a broken link dressed as a guide.

chunks.heading: When a desktop installer is published
chunks.headingPath: Installing the desktop and mobile apps › When a desktop installer is published
chunks.text:
Desktop installers are published as release assets: notarized and stapled `.dmg`
files for macOS, one per architecture for Apple silicon and Intel, signed with a
Developer ID and assessed the way your Mac would assess them. Release assets are
served from the AGI download hosts and GitHub releases, and the download API
refuses anything else.

Stable, beta and nightly are separate release tags. The download page reads
stable.

chunks.heading: Verifying what you downloaded
chunks.headingPath: Installing the desktop and mobile apps › Verifying what you downloaded
chunks.text:
Each release carries a checksum, and the CLI checksums carry a Sigstore
signature. Check the file you downloaded against the published checksum before
running it; the download page shows a verification session end to end.

chunks.heading: What desktop adds once it ships
chunks.headingPath: Installing the desktop and mobile apps › What desktop adds once it ships
chunks.text:
Desktop adds a dedicated managed-cloud account window, approved-folder workflows,
one-step computer-use approvals on supported macOS builds, and the optional Chrome
native bridge. It does not accept provider keys or run local models. Local and BYOK
are available through the released CLI.

chunks.heading: Mobile
chunks.headingPath: Installing the desktop and mobile apps › Mobile
chunks.text:
There is no published mobile release, so Mobile Local mode is not publicly
offered yet. Use the web app on a phone browser in the meantime; the chat
surface, Library, projects and settings all work at phone width.

chunks.heading: In the meantime
chunks.headingPath: Installing the desktop and mobile apps › In the meantime
chunks.text:
Use the web app while waiting for another client. Check each guide for its
platform and setup requirements: access can depend on your plan, workspace
permissions and browser capabilities. The [download page](https://agiworkforce.com/download) is the
place to check current client release availability.

documents.title: Install and set up the CLI

chunks.heading: Getting the binary
chunks.headingPath: Install and set up the CLI › Getting the binary
chunks.text:
The download page carries the current release assets for the `agi` command, one
per architecture, with checksums that carry a Sigstore signature. The CLI page
carries the current install route for your platform.

An npm wrapper is published as `@agiworkforce/cli`. It runs only the matching
`@agiworkforce/cli-<platform>` package, a bundled binary, or the path you set in
`AGI_CLI_BINARY_PATH`; it never falls back to some other `agi` that happens to
be on your PATH. A shell installer and a Homebrew tap are planned and not
published yet, so no command is listed for them.

`agi` is the primary command. `agiworkforce` remains available as a
backward-compatible alias.

chunks.heading: First run
chunks.headingPath: Install and set up the CLI › First run
chunks.text:
```
agi login          # OAuth, or paste a provider API key
agi auth-status    # every configured provider, and how it authenticates
agi --list-models  # what you can actually route to right now
agi exec "what files are in this directory?"
agi                # the interactive terminal UI
```

`agi init` creates `~/.agiworkforce/`, and `agi onboarding` walks the first-time
setup.

chunks.heading: Sessions
chunks.headingPath: Install and set up the CLI › Sessions
chunks.text:
Sessions are resumable. `agi resume` continues a previous session, `agi fork`
branches one, `agi session` inspects them, and `agi history` browses past
sessions. Local sessions never silently leave your device.

chunks.heading: Running work
chunks.headingPath: Install and set up the CLI › Running work
chunks.text:
`agi exec` runs a one-shot prompt and is the form to use in CI. `agi review`
reviews changes, `agi apply` applies the latest diff as a git patch, and
`agi sandbox` runs work under the platform sandbox (Seatbelt, bubblewrap,
Landlock or a Windows restricted token, depending on the OS).

A fallback chain is a comma-separated model list, tried in order, so a cloud
model can fall back to a local one.

chunks.heading: Trust boundaries in the terminal
chunks.headingPath: Install and set up the CLI › Trust boundaries in the terminal
chunks.text:
In the terminal UI, `/privacy-mode` shows the active trust boundary, and moving
to BYOK is an explicit `/continue-with-byok` step, never automatic. There is no
`agi cloud` command: managed runs use the normal model path and fail closed
without an explicit route.

chunks.heading: Managed cloud from the CLI
chunks.headingPath: Install and set up the CLI › Managed cloud from the CLI
chunks.text:
Managed cloud access from the CLI is part of the higher paid tiers. Local mode
and BYOK work on any account, including one with no subscription at all. The
pricing page carries the current details.

chunks.heading: When something is wrong
chunks.headingPath: Install and set up the CLI › When something is wrong
chunks.text:
`agi auth-status` is the first check: it lists every configured provider, so a
missing or expired credential shows up there rather than as a failed run.
`agi features` and `agi execpolicy` report what this build allows.

documents.title: Keyboard shortcuts

chunks.heading: The list
chunks.headingPath: Keyboard shortcuts › The list
chunks.text:
On macOS use Cmd where this says Ctrl.

| Shortcut     | What it does            |
| ------------ | ----------------------- |
| Ctrl+K       | Open search             |
| Ctrl+/       | Show keyboard shortcuts |
| Shift+Ctrl+O | New conversation        |
| Ctrl+B       | Toggle sidebar          |
| Escape       | Focus message composer  |
| Shift+Ctrl+C | Copy last message       |
| Shift+Ctrl+R | Regenerate last message |
| Shift+Ctrl+A | Toggle artifacts panel  |

chunks.heading: Why new chat is Shift and not plain Ctrl+N
chunks.headingPath: Keyboard shortcuts › Why new chat is Shift and not plain Ctrl+N
chunks.text:
Ctrl+N and Cmd+N are reserved by the browser for a new window, so the page never
receives the keypress and nothing can be bound to it. Shift with O is what the
other assistants use for the same reason.

chunks.heading: Turning one off
chunks.headingPath: Keyboard shortcuts › Turning one off
chunks.text:
The shortcuts dialog, opened with Ctrl+/, has a switch per shortcut. A shortcut
you switch off stops firing, it does not merely look disabled, so a binding that
clashes with something else in your setup can be released.

documents.title: Find your files and artifacts in the Library

chunks.heading: What the Library holds
chunks.headingPath: Find your files and artifacts in the Library › What the Library holds
chunks.text:
Everything you uploaded and everything AGI generated for you: documents,
generated files and artifacts, in one list. The tabs across the top are **All**,
**Images**, **Videos**, **Documents**, **Artifacts** and **Generated files**.
Search it by name, and switch between grid and list layout.

chunks.heading: Working with an item
chunks.headingPath: Find your files and artifacts in the Library › Working with an item
chunks.text:
Select a file to preview it. The viewer carries an **Ask about this file** box:
type a question there and it opens a new chat with the file attached and your
question already written. From the item's own menu you can:

- **Add to chat** or **Add to AGI Work**, which stages it for the next session.
- Add it to a project, where it becomes project knowledge for every chat in
  that project.
- Export an artifact as PDF or Word.
- Create a share link for an artifact.

A file too large to preview in place says so and offers a download instead.

chunks.heading: Deleting and restoring
chunks.headingPath: Find your files and artifacts in the Library › Deleting and restoring
chunks.text:
Deleting moves an item to **Recently deleted**, where it stays restorable. For
an uploaded or generated file, that window is 30 days: after it the stored bytes
are removed for good. Other items stay in **Recently deleted** until you restore
them or delete them yourself. A legal hold on your workspace keeps held material
past either window until the hold is released.

**Delete permanently** erases the stored bytes now: nothing restores the file
afterwards and anything linking to it stops resolving, so it asks first and says
so.

chunks.heading: Projects in the Library
chunks.headingPath: Find your files and artifacts in the Library › Projects in the Library
chunks.text:
The Library also lists your projects as folders. Opening one goes to the
project; creating one takes you to the projects page.

chunks.heading: If something is missing
chunks.headingPath: Find your files and artifacts in the Library › If something is missing
chunks.text:
"Nothing here matches that name. Try a shorter search." means the filter, not
the Library, is empty. Clear the search and the filter before concluding a file
is gone. Files attached in a temporary chat never enter the Library by design.

documents.title: Run AGI offline with Local mode

chunks.heading: Running models on your own hardware
chunks.headingPath: Run AGI offline with Local mode › Running models on your own hardware
chunks.text:
The released CLI runs models through Ollama or LM Studio on your own machine.
There are no AGI API keys or managed quotas, and inference can run offline after
the runtime and model are installed. Local mode is free. The current Desktop
application is managed-cloud-only and does not run local models.

chunks.heading: Setting it up
chunks.headingPath: Run AGI offline with Local mode › Setting it up
chunks.text:
1. Install Ollama or LM Studio and at least one compatible model.
2. Install the AGI CLI for your platform.
3. Select the local runtime in the CLI. AGI lists models exposed by the running
   server.

chunks.heading: What stays on your device
chunks.headingPath: Run AGI offline with Local mode › What stays on your device
chunks.text:
In Local mode, conversation content never leaves your device. There is no cloud
sync of local conversations unless you explicitly fork the conversation to another
trust mode, which requires context selection, a payload preview, and your consent.

chunks.heading: Mobile
chunks.headingPath: Run AGI offline with Local mode › Mobile
chunks.text:
AGI Mobile has no published release, so Mobile Local mode is not publicly offered
yet.

documents.title: AGI managed cloud

chunks.heading: Open by default
chunks.headingPath: AGI managed cloud › Open by default
chunks.text:
AGI managed cloud is open by default. Sign in and start: there is no waitlist for
managed cloud and no invite code. Team and Enterprise tiers, with organization
seats, SSO, and admin controls, are the only waitlisted tiers.

chunks.heading: How usage works
chunks.headingPath: AGI managed cloud › How usage works
chunks.text:
Managed cloud usage is metered. Each plan carries a capacity allowance, and the
usage view in Settings shows how much of your current allowance you have used and
when it resets. Usage is reported as a percentage of your allowance and a reset
time.

chunks.heading: Running out of capacity
chunks.headingPath: AGI managed cloud › Running out of capacity
chunks.text:
When your allowance is exhausted, managed cloud requests stop until the allowance
resets. Local mode and BYOK are unaffected by managed-cloud capacity because they do
not run on AGI-operated provider access.

chunks.heading: Where AGI managed cloud data is hosted
chunks.headingPath: AGI managed cloud › Where AGI managed cloud data is hosted
chunks.text:
Hosted data lives in the United States. EU and UK residency hosting is on the
roadmap and is not available today. Local conversations never leave your device in
the first place.

chunks.heading: Training
chunks.headingPath: AGI managed cloud › Training
chunks.text:
AGI does not use customer conversation content to train AGI-owned models.
{{POSITIONING.trustBoundary}}

documents.title: Connect a custom MCP server

chunks.heading: What MCP is here
chunks.headingPath: Connect a custom MCP server › What MCP is here
chunks.text:
MCP (Model Context Protocol) is how AGI talks to a tool server that is not one
of the built-in connectors. A server exposes tools; AGI discovers them and can
call them on your behalf, under the same approval rules as any other connector.

chunks.heading: Adding one
chunks.headingPath: Connect a custom MCP server › Adding one
chunks.text:
A custom MCP connection needs three things: a name to show it under, the
server's URL, and an auth token if the server requires one. AGI then queries the
server for its tools, showing "Discovering live MCP capabilities…" while it
does.

Where a server offers an API key instead, AGI checks how that server accepts a
key before asking you for it, and offers **Test and save** so a bad key fails at
the point you paste it rather than mid-conversation.

chunks.heading: What the discovery results mean
chunks.headingPath: Connect a custom MCP server › What the discovery results mean
chunks.text:
- A list of tools: discovery succeeded and those are what the server offers.
- "The server answered but lists no tools yet." The server is reachable but
  exposes nothing, which is the server's state, not a connection failure.
- "Live tool discovery failed; showing known tools." AGI could not reach the
  server this time and is listing what it saw before. Treat that list as stale.
- "Unavailable during discovery": a tool the server declared but that could not
  be resolved.

chunks.heading: Finding servers
chunks.headingPath: Connect a custom MCP server › Finding servers
chunks.text:
The MCP connector directory is a searchable index of servers. While indexing is
still running it says so, because an incomplete search result would otherwise
read as "no such server".

chunks.heading: Permissions
chunks.headingPath: Connect a custom MCP server › Permissions
chunks.text:
Connecting is not the same as granting scopes. A connector's scope list shows
what it is allowed to reach, its tools see the context you send them, and you
can disconnect at any time. Per-tool approval works the same way as for built-in
connectors.

chunks.heading: Limits
chunks.headingPath: Connect a custom MCP server › Limits
chunks.text:
How many custom MCP connections you can keep depends on your plan; the pricing
page carries the current figures. A workspace administrator can restrict which
connectors a managed workspace permits.

chunks.heading: AGI as an MCP server
chunks.headingPath: Connect a custom MCP server › AGI as an MCP server
chunks.text:
The CLI also runs the other way round: `agi mcp-server` exposes AGI to another
MCP client, so the protocol works in both directions.

documents.title: What AGI remembers, and how to change it

chunks.heading: The three memory switches
chunks.headingPath: What AGI remembers, and how to change it › The three memory switches
chunks.text:
Settings, Memory carries three controls, each doing a different thing:

- **Persistent memory**: "Allow AGI to remember details across conversations."
  With it off, nothing is carried from one conversation to the next.
- **Search past chats**: "Let AGI look up excerpts from your other
  conversations when answering." This reads your history at answer time rather
  than storing facts. It is never used in temporary chats.
- **Allow memory generation from tool-assisted chats**: whether memories may be
  created from chats that used tools, connectors, code or web search.

chunks.heading: Clearing memory
chunks.headingPath: What AGI remembers, and how to change it › Clearing memory
chunks.text:
**Forget everything** deletes all remembered facts. It asks first, because the
facts cannot be recovered afterwards.

chunks.heading: Memory inside a project
chunks.headingPath: What AGI remembers, and how to change it › Memory inside a project
chunks.text:
A project decides for itself whether it draws on account-wide memory. With "Use
memories from outside this project" on, chats there use what has been remembered
account-wide and anything learned there stays in that project. With it off,
chats there use only that project's memories and nothing from your other chats
is included.

chunks.heading: When memory is unavailable in a chat
chunks.headingPath: What AGI remembers, and how to change it › When memory is unavailable in a chat
chunks.text:
If the composer says "Turn on Memory in Settings > Capabilities to use it here",
the capability is switched off for this surface rather than the feature being
broken. Turn it on there and reopen the chat.

chunks.heading: Temporary chats
chunks.headingPath: What AGI remembers, and how to change it › Temporary chats
chunks.text:
A temporary chat neither reads memory nor writes to it. That is part of what
makes it temporary; see the temporary chats article.

documents.title: Pick a model, and control how hard it thinks

chunks.heading: Picking a model by name
chunks.headingPath: Pick a model, and control how hard it thinks › Picking a model by name
chunks.text:
The model control under the composer lists every model your plan and trust mode
make available, grouped and searchable by name. Each entry carries what it can
do: **Vision**, **Tools**, **Search**, **Image output**, **Video output**,
**Reasoning**. Models on your own machine appear under **On this device**.

Leaving the control on **Auto** picks the best model for each message. An
explicit choice is never silently replaced with a different provider.

chunks.heading: What the badges mean
chunks.headingPath: Pick a model, and control how hard it thinks › What the badges mean
chunks.text:
- **Upgrade**: the model exists but your plan does not include it.
- **Coming soon, not yet available**: it is in the catalogue but not live.
- **Unavailable right now**: it is live but not answering at the moment.
- **Auto (free) · community models, capacity varies**: the free routing lane,
  whose capacity is not guaranteed.

chunks.heading: Thinking and effort
chunks.headingPath: Pick a model, and control how hard it thinks › Thinking and effort
chunks.text:
How reasoning is controlled depends on the model. Some have no reasoning
control, some always reason, some expose an on/off **Extended thinking**
switch, some a thinking budget, and some a set of effort levels. The control
under the composer says which applies: "Always on for this model", "Extended
thinking is off for this model", or an effort picker whose hint is "Higher
effort thinks longer before it answers."

chunks.heading: Switching mid-conversation
chunks.headingPath: Pick a model, and control how hard it thinks › Switching mid-conversation
chunks.text:
Within the same trust boundary you can switch models in the middle of a
conversation; the provider label updates before the next request. The control
warns that switching here starts a new prompt cache, so the next message is
processed fresh.

Moving between Local, BYOK and managed cloud is different: it is always an
explicit continuation with context selection, a payload preview, your consent,
and a visible destination label.

chunks.heading: A model that was retired
chunks.headingPath: Pick a model, and control how hard it thinks › A model that was retired
chunks.text:
If a conversation was saved with a model that no longer exists, the chat says so
in place: that model is no longer available, new messages will use the named
replacement, and you can pick a different one. The conversation is not lost and
nothing is rewritten.

chunks.heading: How many there are
chunks.headingPath: Pick a model, and control how hard it thinks › How many there are
chunks.text:
{{MARKETING.models.display}} models across {{MARKETING.providers.display}}
provider integrations. Providers ship and retire models constantly, so the
picker in the product is the current source of truth, never a number in a
document.

documents.title: Privacy controls in Settings

chunks.heading: What is stored where
chunks.headingPath: Privacy controls in Settings › What is stored where
chunks.text:
In Local mode on the CLI, conversations stay on your device and are never
uploaded. CLI BYOK sends requests directly to the provider you select; VS Code
BYOK is coming soon. Web, Mobile, Desktop and Chrome use managed cloud and do not
accept provider keys. Managed cloud conversations are encrypted in transit and
at rest. AGI does not sell your data, and does not use customer conversation
content to train AGI-owned models.

chunks.heading: Diagnostics
chunks.headingPath: Privacy controls in Settings › Diagnostics
chunks.text:
Browser crash reports and consent-gated usage counts help fix bugs. They are
disabled by default and can be turned on or off in Settings, Privacy. Sensitive
request fields are removed before error reports are sent; free-text diagnostic
messages may remain after secrets are masked. Server-side operational error
reporting can run when configured and is not controlled by the browser setting.

chunks.heading: Temporary chats
chunks.headingPath: Privacy controls in Settings › Temporary chats
chunks.text:
"Start new chats as temporary" makes every new conversation temporary: no
message written to your history, no memory, and attachments kept out of the
Library. The conversation record and any attachment are held for up to 30 days
and then removed. An individual conversation can still be switched.

chunks.heading: Your data in the product
chunks.headingPath: Privacy controls in Settings › Your data in the product
chunks.text:
Settings, Privacy gathers the controls in one place: shared links created from
web conversations, archived chats, recently deleted chats, bulk archive and
delete, the files and media you uploaded or AGI generated, memory preferences,
the JSON export, and the privacy requests page for consent and rights requests.

chunks.heading: Where managed cloud data is hosted
chunks.headingPath: Privacy controls in Settings › Where managed cloud data is hosted
chunks.text:
Hosted data lives in the United States. EU and UK residency hosting is on the
roadmap and is not available today. Local conversations never leave your device
in the first place.

chunks.heading: Sessions and devices
chunks.headingPath: Privacy controls in Settings › Sessions and devices
chunks.text:
Session management lives in Settings, Account rather than here: active sessions,
revoking one device, and logging out everywhere. The privacy page links across
to it rather than duplicating the controls.

documents.title: Projects: group chats around shared context

chunks.heading: What a project is
chunks.headingPath: Projects: group chats around shared context › What a project is
chunks.text:
A project holds a set of conversations plus the context they share: a written
set of instructions, uploaded knowledge files, and its own memory scope. Every
chat you start inside a project inherits that context.

chunks.heading: Create one
chunks.headingPath: Projects: group chats around shared context › Create one
chunks.text:
Open the projects page and create a project with a name and, optionally, a
description answering "What are you trying to achieve?". Project settings then
carry four things:

- **Description**: what the project is for.
- **Instructions**: context and how AGI should respond here, for example
  "Respond in Spanish. Reference the latest documentation. Keep answers short."
- **Memory**: a switch for "Use memories from outside this project". On, chats
  here draw on what has been remembered account-wide and anything learned here
  stays in this project. Off, chats here use only this project's memories and
  nothing from your other chats is included.
- **Files**: documents that provide context for every conversation in the
  project.

chunks.heading: Add sources
chunks.headingPath: Projects: group chats around shared context › Add sources
chunks.text:
**Add sources** takes files from your device, text you paste or type, and Google
Drive where that connector is set up. A connector that is not connected yet
shows **Connect in Settings** rather than failing silently.

Each knowledge file reports its own state: **Indexing for search** while it is
being processed, then either full indexing or **Keyword search only**, and
**Not indexed** where it could not be processed. A file that is keyword-only is
still usable; it is matched by words rather than by meaning.

chunks.heading: Shared projects
chunks.headingPath: Projects: group chats around shared context › Shared projects
chunks.text:
If you open a project someone else owns, the sources panel says the owner has
not added any sources yet and that only they can add or remove them. Ownership
of sources does not transfer by sharing.

chunks.heading: Duplicate and delete
chunks.headingPath: Projects: group chats around shared context › Duplicate and delete
chunks.text:
A project can be duplicated, which copies its setup into a new project.
**Delete project** asks first, because the project and its configuration go
with it.

chunks.heading: Limits
chunks.headingPath: Projects: group chats around shared context › Limits
chunks.text:
How many projects and how much knowledge storage you get depends on your plan.
The pricing page carries the current figures.

documents.title: Providers and models

chunks.heading: Which providers are supported
chunks.headingPath: Providers and models › Which providers are supported
chunks.text:
AGI supports {{MARKETING.providers.display}} provider integrations, including
Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, DeepSeek, Perplexity, Qwen, Moonshot, Zhipu, and
custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints. The released CLI supports the Ollama and LM
Studio local runtimes. Desktop runs on your AGI account and does not accept a
provider key or run a local model. The in-product catalog is the current source
of truth.

chunks.heading: How many models
chunks.headingPath: Providers and models › How many models
chunks.text:
{{MARKETING.models.display}} models are available across those providers. The exact
catalogue changes as providers ship and retire models, so the model picker in the
product is the current source of truth.

chunks.heading: Switching model mid-conversation
chunks.headingPath: Providers and models › Switching model mid-conversation
chunks.text:
Within the active trust boundary, you can switch supported models in the middle of
a conversation. The provider label updates before the next request. Moving between
Local, BYOK, and managed Cloud requires an explicit continuation with context
selection, a payload preview, consent, and a visible destination label.

chunks.heading: Automatic routing
chunks.headingPath: Providers and models › Automatic routing
chunks.text:
When the model selection is left on automatic, AGI picks a model for the task from
the models your plan and trust mode make available. An explicit model selection is
never silently replaced with a different provider.

documents.title: Schedule a task, or run it on a trigger

chunks.heading: Create a schedule
chunks.headingPath: Schedule a task, or run it on a trigger › Create a schedule
chunks.text:
The schedules page creates a recurring task from four things: a name,
instructions describing the text task to run, a note on why it runs, and when it
runs. A timezone is part of the schedule, so a daily brief fires at the local
hour you meant. A schedule can be created active or saved inactive and switched
on later.

Schedules can be filtered by project and by status, and each one has a run
history you can open to see what happened on previous runs.

chunks.heading: Triggers instead of a clock
chunks.headingPath: Schedule a task, or run it on a trigger › Triggers instead of a clock
chunks.text:
A schedule can also be attached to an event:

- **Gmail**, which fires when the mailbox changes and waits until the mailbox
  watch is registered for it.
- **Google Calendar**, which waits until the calendar watch is registered.
- **GitHub**, which fires for the repositories your GitHub App installation
  covers.
- **Anything else**, through a signed webhook addressed to its own channel.

A trigger that is still waiting for its watch to register says so rather than
reporting itself as live.

chunks.heading: What an unattended run means
chunks.headingPath: Schedule a task, or run it on a trigger › What an unattended run means
chunks.text:
The form states it plainly: an unattended run can fail or be skipped, and
behaviour may change. Treat a scheduled task as something to check the history
of, not something to rely on silently.

chunks.heading: Editing and deleting
chunks.headingPath: Schedule a task, or run it on a trigger › Editing and deleting
chunks.text:
Editing a schedule warns before discarding unsaved changes. **Delete Schedule**
asks first, and deleting a trigger is a separate confirmation.

chunks.heading: Limits
chunks.headingPath: Schedule a task, or run it on a trigger › Limits
chunks.text:
How many scheduled tasks you can keep depends on your plan, and free and
BYOK-only accounts have none. A workspace administrator can turn Schedules and
Event triggers off for a managed workspace. The pricing page carries the current
per-plan figures.

documents.title: Search: the web, your chats and the help centre

chunks.heading: Searching the web from a chat
chunks.headingPath: Search: the web, your chats and the help centre › Searching the web from a chat
chunks.text:
There is no search switch to find. Managed web search is ambient: it stays on
whenever the selected model and deployment have a real search path, and turns
off only when no such path exists. The composer states whether search is on for
the model you picked. `/search` in the composer states the intent explicitly for
a single message.

Managed cloud search follows the chat and usage policy for your plan. In Local
and BYOK the behaviour depends on the runtime and provider you selected.

chunks.heading: Deep Research
chunks.headingPath: Search: the web, your chats and the help centre › Deep Research
chunks.text:
**Deep Research** is a separate composer mode for multi-step investigation
rather than a single answer. It is not available on every model: choosing one
that cannot do it says "Deep Research isn't available for this model. Choose
Auto or a model that supports Deep Research." Availability also depends on your
plan, and an ineligible plan shows "Upgrade to use Deep Research".

chunks.heading: Finding your own conversations
chunks.headingPath: Search: the web, your chats and the help centre › Finding your own conversations
chunks.text:
Cmd/Ctrl+K opens search across your messages and conversations. It searches
message text as well as titles, filters by date, and marks results that came
from a code session or a project source. Your recent searches are kept; clearing
them warns that it cannot be undone.

chunks.heading: Letting AGI search your past chats
chunks.headingPath: Search: the web, your chats and the help centre › Letting AGI search your past chats
chunks.text:
Settings, Memory holds **Search past chats**: "Let AGI look up excerpts from
your other conversations when answering." It is never used in temporary chats.

chunks.heading: Searching the help centre
chunks.headingPath: Search: the web, your chats and the help centre › Searching the help centre
chunks.text:
The help page carries a search box over everything published here. It is plain
keyword retrieval over the published pages, with no model call, so it keeps
working even when the support assistant is off. If nothing matches, it says so
rather than guessing, and points at contact@agiworkforce.com.

documents.title: Share a conversation or an artifact

chunks.heading: Create a share link
chunks.headingPath: Share a conversation or an artifact › Create a share link
chunks.text:
Open the conversation's menu and choose **Share conversation**. Two audiences
are offered:

- **Anyone with the link**, described as best for a quick review.
- **Share with workspace**, for longer collaboration, which limits the link to
  members of your workspace.

Once the link exists the dialog confirms the audience: "Anyone with the link can
open this now", or "Only your workspace can open this now". Copy it from the
dialog, or open the link to check what a reader sees.

chunks.heading: Change or revoke a link
chunks.headingPath: Share a conversation or an artifact › Change or revoke a link
chunks.text:
Switching the audience after the fact asks first, naming the change: "Make this
readable by anyone with the link?" or "Limit this to your workspace?".
**Revoke share** removes access, and the confirmation says that anyone using the
link will immediately lose access.

chunks.heading: Find every link you have created
chunks.headingPath: Share a conversation or an artifact › Find every link you have created
chunks.text:
Settings, **Shared links** lists the links created from web conversations, with
the ones marked _Workspace only_ distinguished from public ones, and revokes any
of them. Published artifacts have their own list in Settings with an
**Unpublish artifact** action.

chunks.heading: Export instead of sharing
chunks.headingPath: Share a conversation or an artifact › Export instead of sharing
chunks.text:
The conversation menu also exports. From the Library, an artifact exports as PDF
or Word. There is no spreadsheet export on web, so no xlsx option is offered
rather than one that would fail after you picked it.

chunks.heading: Chats you cannot share
chunks.headingPath: Share a conversation or an artifact › Chats you cannot share
chunks.text:
A temporary chat cannot be shared while the control is on, because it is never
saved. Turn temporary chat off first.

documents.title: Create an account and send your first message

chunks.heading: Create the account
chunks.headingPath: Create an account and send your first message › Create the account
chunks.text:
1. Open the sign-up page and enter the email address you want the account under.
2. Choose how you sign up: **Continue with Google**, **Continue with GitHub**, or
   an email address and a password.
3. If you used email, confirm the code sent to your inbox. If the code has not
   arrived, check the spam folder before requesting another.

There is no checkbox to tick. The sign-up screen states that by signing up you
agree to the Terms of Use and acknowledge the Privacy Policy, and completing
sign-up is the agreement.

chunks.heading: What you can do immediately
chunks.headingPath: Create an account and send your first message › What you can do immediately
chunks.text:
Managed cloud is open by default. A new account can open the chat surface and
send a message straight away: there is no waitlist for managed cloud and no
invite code to redeem. Team and Enterprise tiers are the waitlisted ones.

chunks.heading: Send the first message
chunks.headingPath: Create an account and send your first message › Send the first message
chunks.text:
Open the chat surface, type into the composer, and press Enter. The composer
placeholder reads "Ask anything. Type / for commands". Below the composer the
model selector shows which model will answer; leaving it on **Auto** lets AGI
pick a model for each message from the ones your plan and trust mode allow.

chunks.heading: If sign-up does not complete
chunks.headingPath: Create an account and send your first message › If sign-up does not complete
chunks.text:
- "No account uses this email. Sign up instead." on a sign-in screen means the
  address has never been registered. Sign up rather than resetting a password.
- "That password is too common." means the password was rejected against a
  common-password list. Choose a longer, less common one.
- A verification step the sign-up screen cannot render ends with "This account
  needs a verification step we cannot show here yet." Email
  contact@agiworkforce.com and a person will unblock the account.

documents.title: Temporary chats

chunks.heading: What a temporary chat does
chunks.headingPath: Temporary chats › What a temporary chat does
chunks.text:
A temporary chat stays out of your history, your memory and your Library. It is
never written to your conversation history, nothing said in it is remembered
across conversations, files you attach do not land in your Library, and a
connector asks before every call even where you saved "Always allow".

A connector call still reaches that service, and that service keeps its own
record. Temporary is about what AGI keeps, not about what the outside world
forgets.

What AGI does keep is narrow and bounded. No message of a temporary chat is
written to your conversation history. The conversation record itself, and any
file you attach, are held for up to 30 days and then removed, which is what
keeps an in-flight chat working and an attachment readable while you are still
in it. A legal hold placed on your workspace keeps that material past the 30
days until the hold is released.

chunks.heading: Turning it on
chunks.headingPath: Temporary chats › Turning it on
chunks.text:
The composer carries a **Temporary chat** control for the conversation you are
in. To make every new conversation temporary, turn on "Start new chats as
temporary" in Settings, Privacy.

chunks.heading: Ending one
chunks.headingPath: Temporary chats › Ending one
chunks.text:
**End temporary chat** discards it. The confirmation states the consequence
plainly: a temporary chat is never written to your history, so ending it is the
end of it, every message goes on this device and any other, and nobody can
reopen or restore it. Copy out anything you still need before you confirm.

chunks.heading: What you cannot do with one
chunks.headingPath: Temporary chats › What you cannot do with one
chunks.text:
A temporary chat cannot be shared. The share control refuses with "A temporary
chat cannot be shared. Turn off temporary chat to keep it, then share it." Turn
the control off first, which starts saving the conversation, and then share it.

documents.title: Approvals: what a tool may do without asking

chunks.heading: The account-wide default
chunks.headingPath: Approvals: what a tool may do without asking › The account-wide default
chunks.text:
Settings carries one **Default approval for tool actions** with two settings:

- **Ask before every action.** Every connector, plugin and tool action waits for
  your approval, including actions that only read data. This is the default.
- **Run read-only actions without asking.** Actions that only read data, search
  the web, fetch a page, or run code in the AGI sandbox run on their own.
  Anything that writes, deletes, sends, buys, changes credentials, or runs on
  your own machine still asks, and so does every connector tool AGI does not
  know.

The setting syncs to your account, so it holds wherever you are signed in.

chunks.heading: Per-tool permissions
chunks.headingPath: Approvals: what a tool may do without asking › Per-tool permissions
chunks.text:
Each connector has a **Tool Permissions** panel that overrides the default for
one tool at a time: **Always run without asking**, **Needs approval each time**,
or **Never run this tool**. **Reset all to default** clears every override for
that connector and asks first.

chunks.heading: Approving in the moment
chunks.headingPath: Approvals: what a tool may do without asking › Approving in the moment
chunks.text:
When a tool runs for the first time, AGI asks. Choosing **Always allow** saves
that verdict so the same tool can run without prompting again. A temporary chat
ignores saved "Always allow" verdicts and asks every time.

chunks.heading: Checking what ran
chunks.headingPath: Approvals: what a tool may do without asking › Checking what ran
chunks.text:
**Recent calls** on a connector is its call log: what was called and when. A
connector that has never been called says so rather than showing an empty table
that could be read as a failure.

chunks.heading: Removing a connector clears its approvals
chunks.headingPath: Approvals: what a tool may do without asking › Removing a connector clears its approvals
chunks.text:
Removing a connector deactivates it and clears its saved "Always allow" tool
permissions at the same time, so a later reconnect starts from a clean approval
state. It also asks the provider to revoke every account you connected through
that connector, not only the one AGI treated as the default, and deletes the
credentials AGI held for them.

documents.title: Troubleshooting: when something does not work

chunks.heading: Start here
chunks.headingPath: Troubleshooting: when something does not work › Start here
chunks.text:
Most failures name themselves on screen. Read the message before changing
anything: AGI distinguishes "this is switched off", "your plan does not include
this", "this model cannot do this" and "this is broken", and the fix is
different for each.

Check the status page before investigating your own account.

chunks.heading: A chat will not load
chunks.headingPath: Troubleshooting: when something does not work › A chat will not load
chunks.text:
"Chat could not be displayed" with **Try again** is a render failure; your
messages are already saved, so retrying or opening another conversation loses
nothing. "You are offline" means the browser lost its connection: reconnect and
try again.

chunks.heading: A message will not send
chunks.headingPath: Troubleshooting: when something does not work › A message will not send
chunks.text:
- "Your previous message was still starting, so this one is back here. Send it
  again." Send it once more; nothing was lost.
- "Your queued message was not sent: you switched chats before the reply
  finished." It was saved as a draft in the original chat. Its attachments were
  not kept, so re-attach them.
